camera.trait: On the job: the same eye for timing and framing goes into the media & design work at Guards HQ.
camera.label: Photography
camera.blurb: I shoot the moments most people scroll past: the quiet in-between frames at events, on the street, and around Singapore. What started as documenting friends turned into a real obsession with light, timing and composition.

watch.trait: On the job: keeping the record. Service histories here, documentation and audit trails at work.
watch.label: Watches
watch.blurb: Mechanical watches run in the family. I grew up around a small collection that got passed down and added to over three generations, each piece carrying a story about who wore it and why. Somewhere along the way I became the one keeping the record.

cards.trait: On the job: drill it until it's repeatable. Same instinct behind the trading playbooks.
cards.label: Card throwing
cards.blurb: I found card throwing down a late-night rabbit hole and never climbed back out. It's equal parts physics and patience (grip, spin, release), and there's a strange calm in drilling the same throw a hundred times until it finally bites the target.

monitors.label: The trading screens
monitors.blurb: Charts, scanners and the pre-market report the trading workflow writes every morning. This is where the Finance lens comes from.

work.label: The desk
work.blurb: Enough downtime. This is where the trading, building and analysis happen. Step back into the professional portfolio.

trophy.trait: On the job: years of training for a few minutes on the mat or the board. Discipline compounds.
trophy.label: Trophy cabinet
trophy.blurb: Two sports, years of each. Taekwondo on the mat, diving off the board, and the medals that stuck around.

taekwondo.name: Trained under Grandmaster Kang Shin Chul

photography.name: Reginald Tan
photography.bio: Singapore. Events, street, and the occasional portrait. Shot on whatever's in my bag.

entries.line2: My grandfather's first mechanical — a hand-wound dress watch bought with his first proper paycheck.
A steel diver that survived the shipyard, the sea, and two decades of being worn every single day.
The dress watch moves to my father. He wears it to his own first job — and starts the habit of keeping notes on each piece.
The first automatic joins the drawer. No more winding. The collection quietly doubles over the decade.
I inherit the diver. Scratched, honest, still ticking — and I fall for the mechanics of the thing.
I maintain them all now: service history, stories, who wore what. A small archive that keeps on running.

cards.title: Card Toss
cards.intro: Drag back on the card, aim, and release to throw. Land it in the target rings — bullseye scores highest. Swirl the card before you release for a curveball bonus. Ten cards. See how sharp your flick is.
